summary: The role of the consular officer is limited to providing information obtained from foreign officials on requirements for local marriages and performing notarial and authentication services.
quote:
a. The role of the consular officer is now limited to
providing information obtained from foreign officials on requirements for local
marriages and performing notarial and authentication services.

scope_text: Prior to November 9, 1989, when requested to do so, and when one of the contracting parties was a U.S. citizen
scope_quotes:
b. Prior to November 9, 1989, consular officers, when
requested to do so, could make certain that foreign marriages were effective
for purposes of U.S. law by acting as official witnesses to the marriage, when
one of the contracting parties was a U.S. citizen, pursuant to the authority of
Section 31 of the Act of June 22, 1860 (12 Stat. 79; 22 U.S.C. 4192). The Act
also provided for issuance of an official certificate of witness to such
marriage.

quote:
c.  Section 31 was repealed, effective February 16,
1990, by Section 123 of the FY 1990-1991 Foreign Affairs Authorization Act.

references: Section 31 of the Act of June 22, 1860
summary: Certificates of Witness to Marriage, issued by consular officers pursuant to Section 31 of the Act of June 22, 1860, prior to its repeal, remain valid; such certificates, using the most recent edition of Form FS-87, were issued from when it was revised in October 1939 until November 9, 1989.
quote:
d. Certificates of Witness to Marriage, issued by
consular officers pursuant to Section 31 of the Act of June 22, 1860, prior to
its repeal, remain valid. Such certificates, using the most recent edition of
Form FS-87, were issued from when it was revised in October 1939, until
November 9, 1989.

summary: You cannot make any official certification about the status or eligibility to marry of persons residing in the United States who propose to be married abroad, or about the laws of the United States or of any of the fifty States or Territories about eligibility for marriage or the solemnization of a marriage.
